definition: OMI is a source-available AI pendant that listens to conversations and makes them searchable later. It is budget source-available hardware.
extendedDescription:
OMI takes the open route to wearables. The hardware listens throughout your day, and the source-available software turns those conversations into a searchable record you control.

Because it is source-available, you can inspect what it does with your audio and run parts of it yourself. That transparency is rare in a category built on always-on microphones.

Capture is only half the job. OMI remembers what was said. It does not draft the follow-up email, create the task, or update the calendar. Recall without action still leaves you the to-do list.

faqs.answer: OMI is budget-priced open hardware, and the software is source-available for inspection and self-hosting.
faqs.question: How much does OMI cost?

faqs.answer: Yes. OMI is source-available, so you can inspect the code and self-host parts of it. That is a real privacy advantage over closed wearables.
faqs.question: Is OMI really source-available?

howGaiaUsesIt: GAIA respects the source-available ethos and shares it: GAIA is source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) and self-hostable via Docker. Where OMI stops at recall, GAIA continues into action, turning captured context into drafted emails, created tasks, and scheduled events across 50+ integrations.
